# Hand off exportable files through Wants with appropriate URI access

## Platform difference

Launching a receiving app may require a readable file URI and access grant rather than passing a remote URL or private filesystem string.

## Implementation

Kazumi writes an M3U8 wrapper and invokes viewData with read-URI permission and a receiver chooser; its Dart path is enabled only when a Referer header is unnecessary. Bugaoshan creates an ICS file and exposes it through the native calendar import channel. Nomark persists audio in private files storage before invoking system sharing.

## Applicability

The receiver must exist and support the MIME/action/data contract. Direct calendar-plugin operations, such as NJU uses, are a separate integration path with their own permission/API checks.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

Channel success may mean the handoff was attempted, not that another app accepted or consumed the content. Preserve files for the receiver long enough and account for rejected or cancelled requests.

## Verification

Test installed/missing receivers, read access, cancellation, MIME/extension correctness, cleanup timing and URLs requiring authentication headers.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
